title: The Ember of the Weeping Wood
premise: Vesper Marchetti has spent their whole life in the Weeping Wood valley, where the old gods' magic cannot reach, carving bones that whisper the names of the dead. When prayers begin to be answered again and the dead fall silent one by one, Vesper learns the god-thing wearing King Aldric's crown is devouring souls to rebuild itself—and Vesper's own bone-carving gift is the key it needs. Joined by a disgraced priestess, a deserter knight, and the ghost of a murdered prince, Vesper must cross into the god-touched world they were hidden from as a child. In the end, Veper unbinds Aldric by offering their own hearing of the dead as payment, going deaf to the whispers forever but freeing the king—and discovering that the found family they made along the way hears them now instead.
about_author: Noor Okonkwo is a former mortuary archivist who writes fantasy about grief, duty, and the stubborn persistence of love. They live between Lagos and Lisbon with two cats named after minor saints.

chapters.title: The Valley Where Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Introduces the bone-carver's trade: carving names into the dead so their whispers can rest. A traveler's corpse arrives with no name at all—its soul already eaten. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine; Vesper realizes something outside the valley has changed.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: Priestess Sable's POV. She fled her order when the gods went silent; now candles relight themselves and her abandoned prayers are answered by something hungry wearing a familiar voice. She arrives in the valley seeking sanctuary. Emotional beat: terror disguised as hope—the danger of getting what you asked for.

chapters.title: What the Bones Refuse to Say
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The nameless dead multiply; Vesper's carvings crack mid-work for the first time. Sable recognizes the soul-hunger's signature: the crown-god of King Aldric has woken. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance—two people who each thought they were the last sane one.

chapters.title: The Deserter at the Ford
chapters.summary: Knight Corvin Hale's POV. He deserted Aldric's army after witnessing the king speak to his own shadow. Hunted, he stumbles into the valley and begs asylum, bringing news: the king marches here, seeking 'the carver.' Emotional beat: shame met with unexpected grace; the found family begins to form.

chapters.title: A Prince Among Whispers
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Carving a royal femur recovered from the border, Vesper wakes Prince Ilan—Aldric's murdered heir—who reveals the crown-thing killed him and wears his father like a glove. It wants Vesper because valley-born bone-silence is the one substance it cannot digest or control. Emotional beat: grief turning to purpose; Vesper accepts they must leave.

chapters.title: Crossing the Threshold
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The four slip past the valley's warding stones on the night of the new moon, entering a world where magic answers every stray thought. Sable's old faith floods back painfully. Emotional beat: wonder laced with loss—the valley's silence was also a kind of safety, and it is gone forever.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Ambushed by crown-pilgrims whose eyes have gone milk-white, the group survives only through Ilan's ghost-guidance and Corvin's willingness to kill again. Vesper and Sable share a firelit confession of what duty cost them both. Emotional beat: love against duty crystallizes—each choosing the other over the mission's clean logic.

chapters.title: The Court of the Hollow King
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Infiltrating the capital during a feast of thanksgiving, they see Aldric up close: a man flickering inside his own body like a candle in wind. The crown-thing senses Vesper and offers a bargain—Vesper's silence-gift in exchange for sparing the valley. Emotional beat: temptation; survival offered at exactly the price Vesper swore never to pay.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Sable and Corvin's alternating POV. While Sable performs a forbidden rite to hold the crown-thing's attention and Corvin holds the door against pilgrims, Vesper carves Aldric's true name into his own living bone, severing the bond. The thing turns on Vesper fully. Emotional beat: climax—sacrifice chosen freely, family fighting as one body.

chapters.title: The Ember That Remains
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper gives up the hearing of the dead to starve the crown-thing into nothing; Aldric wakes weeping over his son's grave-marker, which Vesper carved with Ilan's whispered blessing. Deaf to ghosts but surrounded by the living who stayed, Vesper returns to a valley that is no longer hiding—only home. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; the price was paid, and it was worth it.
